items.title: Iran / Strait of Hormuz escalation
items.detail: US struck 80+ targets in Iran overnight after attacks on three commercial vessels; Iranian oil-export waivers revoked. Brent +3% to ~$76.50 with the SPR at its weakest since 1983. Roughly a fifth of world oil transits the strait — any move toward closure is an inflation shock the Fed can't ease into.

items.title: Memory/semis in a bear market within the AI trade
items.detail: MU, Samsung, SK Hynix and the memory ETF are >20% off highs; semis have lost ~$1.5T of market value since Jun 25. Samsung's 19x profit jump and Micron's +346% y/y revenue were sold — when blowout numbers get sold, the market is repricing the cycle top, not the quarter. No bottom-fishing on day two.

items.title: AI-capex concentration
items.detail: Overnight selloff was explicitly attributed to stretched AI valuations and demand doubts. Q2 hyperscaler capex guidance remains the single swing factor for Tech and the adjacent power/industrial trades — AI-heavy books carry correlated exposure across chips, cooling, and generation names.

items.title: Rates backing up on oil
items.detail: 10Y at 4.56%, a one-month high, as the oil spike feeds inflation expectations. Higher discount rates pressure exactly the long-duration growth names that dominate this tape; a 10Y above 4.75% would force a broader de-rate.

items.title: Vol regime shift
items.detail: VIX +15.5% in a session, 15.57 → 18.63. Yesterday's complacency warning is triggering: hedges are no longer cheap, and low-vol-regime unwinds tend to run further than the first headline. Respect stops; don't add size into rising vol.

items.title: FOMC minutes + inflation optics
items.detail: Minutes due today with the Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75%. An oil-driven CPI impulse narrows the path to easing while growth data (June payrolls +57k) is already soft — the stagflation-lite combination the tape handles worst.

items.title: Credit still calm
items.detail: HY spreads were tight (~2.75% OAS) at last check and the curve is positive (+0.42%). Zero of nine recession-checklist items triggered. Until credit confirms, this is a headline correction, not a cycle turn.

items.title: Q2 earnings season starts next week
items.detail: Banks kick off mid-July. Q1's pattern — beats rewarded less, misses punished disproportionately — argues against carrying oversized single-name positions into prints, especially in AI-linked names where the capex question hangs over every call.
